newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add reserves via 2-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add reserves via 2-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will add temporary reserves to the banking system on Tuesday, probably through two-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.

"We've got some notable pressure because of the year-end coming up and the Fed will try to counter that," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. "We're looking for a rather aggressive reserve addition -- probably two-day (system repurchases) after Monday's seven-day operation -- to counter the reserve pressures."
Federal funds opened at seven percent on Tuesday and slipped to 6-1/2 percent in early trade.
The Fed's target for the funds rate is 5-1/4 percent.
"Volatility is the watchword for the funds market today," said William Sullivan, senior vice president and director of money market research at Dean Witter Reynolds.

"We opened at 7.0 percent and, as always, the final trading day of the calendar year will be volatile in the funds market," said Sullivan. "Fed funds traded as high as 15 percent on Monday and that set the stage for today when we not only have year-end pressures, but also (bank reserve maintenance) period-end pressures that include the settlement of the two- and five-year notes (that the Treasury sold last week)."
Sullivan said the Fed would add temporary reserves to the banking system through term system repurchase agreements.

Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International, concurred, citing period- and year-end pressures as well as reserve demand tied to the settlement of the two- and five-year notes that the Treasury sold last week.
